items.review_rationale: Read the relative-base-change quantifier in this definition: all continuous maps Z→Y are permitted, and the induced projection X×_Y Z→Z must be closed. Do not equate this with merely closed original f, or only external products Z×f.

references.context: Topology: closed map sending every topologically closed subset to a closed subset

references.phrase: topological fibre product with subspace topology
references.context: Topology: pullback of topological spaces over common target Y

references.disposition: No restriction to discrete or compact Z; the closedness condition is stable under all displayed base changes.

items.review_rationale: Reviewed a binary categorical product via its object P, two projection arrows, and unique mediating arrow for every pair of maps into X and Y. This is not necessarily Cartesian product of underlying sets.

references.context: Category theory: binary product cone consisting of two arrows with common domain

references.phrase: for every object Z and arrows f,g a unique h exists
references.disposition: The uniqueness of the induced h commuting with both projections is the universal product property, not mere existence of P.

items.review_rationale: Inspected all terms of the graded-map criterion and the M/JM coefficient module, quotient ring R/J, polynomial variables, and J-adic associated graded pieces. Unlike M-regularity, quasi-regularity is defined here by a graded isomorphism and is not silently identified with an M-regular sequence.

references.phrase: quotient ring R/J and quotient module M/JM
references.context: Commutative algebra: quotient ring and module by an ideal action
Commutative algebra: polynomial algebra in finitely many indeterminates over quotient ring
Commutative algebra: associated graded module of J-adic filtration

references.phrase: graded isomorphism of the displayed canonical map
references.context: Graded commutative algebra: grading-preserving module isomorphism identifying variables with classes f_i

references.disposition: A specific graded comparison map is required to be an isomorphism; ordinary finite generation of J is insufficient.

items.review_rationale: Read catenarity across any comparable primes, using maximal finite prime chains connecting the endpoints and the stated boundedness of their possible lengths. This condition does not require R to be Noetherian.

references.context: Order theory: saturated finite chain under prime-ideal inclusion between fixed endpoints

references.phrase: all maximal finite chains have equal length and lengths are bounded above
references.disposition: Both equal-length and bounded-length clauses are explicitly stated; no Noetherian hypothesis is silently imposed.

items.review_rationale: Read the universal criterion over every finitely generated R-algebra, distinct from catenarity of the base ring alone and from base change to only finite or field extensions.

references.disposition: Quantification covers all finite-type R-algebras, not just finite integral ring extensions.

items.review_rationale: Reviewed the geometric integrality of k-algebra A with base field extension K/k arbitrary; the tensor-product K-algebra must remain an integral domain for every such extension, not merely A reduced or geometrically reduced.

references.context: Commutative algebra: commutative field-algebra A with extension of scalars to K via tensor product

references.disposition: Arbitrary field extensions are quantified, including transcendental extensions; the condition includes nonzero domain requirement.

items.review_rationale: Reviewed the equivalent algebraic-closure test for geometric integrality; it is a single specified tensor-extension test over k-bar and is a variant of the same existing meaning rather than another new mathematical object.

references.context: Commutative algebra: induced algebra structure on A⊗_k k-bar

references.disposition: This condition is a second formulation of geometric integrality and does not replace algebraic closure by any arbitrary finite extension.

items.review_rationale: Read the strict-map comparison of two topologies on the image f(X): quotient topology induced by X and subspace topology induced by Y. This need not require f to be globally surjective onto Y.

references.phrase: quotient topology induced by surjection X→f(X)
references.context: Topology: final quotient topology associated with a surjection onto its set-theoretic image

references.disposition: Equality is required on the image, not on all of Y; the map need not be surjective onto Y.
